title: E0047: Resource lifecycle leak
plain_english: This rule reports function-scoped resources that are opened and never closed or transferred to another owner. It complements E0043, which reports use-after-close and double-close on tracked streams.
why_matters: Leaving file handles, pipes, process handles, or directory handles open can exhaust system resources, especially in long-running workers or code paths that run many times. Closing resources explicitly, or transferring ownership clearly, makes resource lifetimes easier to reason about.
bad_example:
<?php
function write(string $path, string $data): void
{
    $h = fopen($path, 'w');
    fwrite($h, $data);
    // missing fclose($h)
}
good_example:
<?php
function write(string $path, string $data): void
{
    $h = fopen($path, 'w');
    if ($h === false) {
        return;
    }
    try {
        fwrite($h, $data);
    } finally {
        fclose($h);
    }
}
what_it_checks: `fopen()`, `fsockopen()`, `pfsockopen()`, `stream_socket_client()`, and `tmpfile()` handles that should be closed with `fclose()`
`popen()` handles that should be closed with `pclose()`
`proc_open()` handles that should be closed with `proc_close()`
`opendir()` handles that should be closed with `closedir()`
